name: Ferocitas the Dream Eater
summary: In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot sends you north to recover an emerald stolen by Gnarlpine furbolgs. Their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater, wears it around his neck.

sections.title: A Defiled Heirloom
sections.body:
Tallonkai Swiftroot was relieved when his dreamcatcher returned from the corrupted wilds. Then he saw its ruined state. The sacred artifact had been vandalized, and its emerald centerpiece pried from the woven frame.

Night elves spoke of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze Village, fallen under the sway of their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater. He wore a brilliant green stone around his neck. The gem was useless and perverse in Ferocitas's clutches, so Tallonkai sent defenders to reclaim it.

sections.title: Purging the Mystics
sections.body: The Gnarlpine furbolgs in northern Teldrassil were once peaceful neighbors. Corruption from the World Tree drove them into frenzy and madness. Their mystics once practiced harmonious nature rites, but now draw on distorted magical energies. You can reach Ferocitas by cutting through the mystics guarding his woodland enclave. Return the jewel to Tallonkai, so he can make his dreamcatcher whole and restore balance to the woods.

faq.q: Where do I find Ferocitas the Dream Eater?
faq.answer: Ferocitas the Dream Eater waits in the forest north of Starbreeze Village on Teldrassil, among corrupted Gnarlpine mystics and other woodland hazards.
Ferocitas leads the Gnarlpine furbolgs and commands corrupted mystics north of Starbreeze Village. He took the emerald from Tallonkai Swiftroot's dreamcatcher and made it into a crude necklace.

faq.q: Why does Tallonkai Swiftroot want the jewel back?
faq.answer: Tallonkai Swiftroot wants the emerald back because it is the core power source of his dreamcatcher. Without it, the talisman cannot be repaired or channel the Emerald Dream's protective energies.

faq.q: Can the Gnarlpine actually use the emerald's magic?
faq.answer: No. Tallonkai Swiftroot says the emerald's magic is useless to Ferocitas and the Gnarlpine mystics. They coveted it only as a glowing bauble.
This is the final chapter of a two-part chain that began with The Emerald Dreamcatcher. Deliver the jewel to Tallonkai in Dolanaar, and he can repair his heirloom.

faq.q: Why are the Gnarlpine mystics hostile?
faq.answer: A strange corruption in the boughs of the newly planted World Tree has affected much of Teldrassil's wildlife and furbolg tribes. It twisted the Gnarlpine's minds and made them aggressive.

angles.text: As a night elf defending Teldrassil, you see the tragedy in the Gnarlpine mystics' corruption and theft of sacred talismans. The Gnarlpine were once allies of the Kaldorei.
As a druid, you know dreamcatchers are potent instruments tied to the Emerald Dream. A corrupted furbolg has defiled one, and nature calls for swift retribution.
